projects.title: Ninja Academy
projects.description:
Team PewPewPew, a team of 7, worked with EA Games's Office of the Chief Creative Officer (OCCO) to develop a game for EA’s new connected TV platform. PewPewPew’s challenge was to develop one of the first family-friendly shooter games for the platform’s action channel where players can use any mobile device as a controller.

I was a programmer and game designer for the team. For programming, I worked on prototyping control schemes, architecting how data is passed throughout the project, avatars, level flow, boss mechanics, projectiles, and scoreboards, as well as touching almost every other piece of code written by the other programmers on the team. For game design, I worked with the artists to decide on enemy animations and environments, enemy and boss stats/abilities/movement patterns, and did the placement of all the levels including enemy spawns and movement paths using a NavMesh.

projects.title: TF-CBT: Triangle of Life
projects.description:
Traumatic experiences often leave negative after-effects in children. This can cause recurring negative thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. Our client, the Allegheny Singer Research Institute/Disruptive Health Technology Institute, takes these children through a program called TF-CBT, Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, to inform and help them recover. Team Transcendence, a team of 6, assisted the TF-CBT by creating a game to augment the therapy. TF-CBT: Triangle of Life is a mobile game that will teach traumatized children about the Cognitive Triangle of thoughts, feelings, and behaviors, as well as how to replace their negative thoughts with positive ones.

On this project I was lead programmer and game designer. For programming, I created all of the in-game movement and platformer systems including moving platforms and item collection. For game design, I worked mostly on level design, animal interactions, how we progress through levels, how cognitive triangle interactions worked, and also helped with dialogue.

The game received an Honorable Mention from PEACEapp. More info at: http://www.cmu.edu/news/stories/archives/2015/february/transcendence.html
